messages.subject: D-RUG this week Thurs 1-3
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

This week at D-RUG Kara Moore O'Leary will be talking about the popbio package which constructs and analyzes projection matrix models. Kara will present examples from her own work projecting the demographics of a rare native CA perennial plant along with some of her own tweaks.

If you took Marissa and Sebastians's course last quarter, the popbio package has tools to automate and streamline a lot of the methods they taught.

D-RUG this quarter will be held Thursdays 1-3PM in Wickson 2124.

Noam

messages.subject: D-RUG today 1-3 in Wickson 2124
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

A reminder that the first D-RUG work session of the quarter will be today 1-3PM in Wickson 2124.  Kara Moore O'Leary will be be presenting on the popbio package and how she uses it in her work on rare plant demographics.

Also, R version 3.0.0 was released this week.  Bring your questions about upgrading and new features (or e-mail the list with them if you can't make it).  If there are enough, we may compile a FAQ / upgrade guide.

Noam

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Histogram for frequency distribution separated by year (3years)
messages.subject_clean: [D-RUG]: Histogram for frequency distribution separated by year (3years)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Pedro,

You can use ggplot to make a histogram like this very easily.  The following command assumes that data is in a data frame called "data" where your columns are "Year" and "DiseaseIndex", and each row represents one observation,
require(ggplot2)
ggplot(data, aes(x=DiseaseIndex, fill=Year)) + geom_histogram(binwidth=.5, position="dodge")

See http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/Plotting_distributions_(ggplot2)/ for some more examples and variations.

Noam

messages.subject: D-RUG topics
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I just wanted to put a call out for anyone who wants to present a topic at D-RUG.  Remember - talks don't have to be tutorials, we're happy for people to present case studies of their work for feedback, as well!

In the survey at the beginning of the quarter, a few people requested a talk on mixed models and specifically the `bbmle` package.  Anyone interested in tackling this?  Stella Copeland gave an intro to mixed models in the fall (See here: http://goo.gl/s1MCK), but we have lots of new users so it would be great if someone were interested.

Here are the upcoming topics for the next three weeks:

 - Speeding up your code (Noam)
 - Parallel processing (Jacob Teter)
 - Spatial analysis tools (Robert J. Hijmans)

We'll probably also have a session on creating R packages towards the end of the quarter.

Noam
